abstract: ARM Debug Interface v5 (ADIv5) defines the standardized debug-access architecture used by all Arm Cortex-M, Cortex-R, and Cortex-A SoCs. SWD is the 2-wire variant of the same Debug Access Port (DAP) — SWDIO (bidirectional data) + SWCLK (host-driven clock) replace the 4-wire JTAG TAP (TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO) used by ADIv5's JTAG-DP variant. SWJ-DP (Serial Wire / JTAG Debug Port) is a mode-switchable controller that supports both protocols and selects between them via a 16-bit JTAG-to-SWD or SWD-to-JTAG selection sequence. Above the DP layer, ADIv5 defines an Access Port (AP) bus with up to 256 APs selected via the APSEL register; the most common AP is MEM-AP (memory-mapped access to the SoC's debug bus), and JTAG-AP forwards transactions to downstream legacy JTAG TAPs. CoreSight ROM Tables published at the MEM-AP BASE address enumerate the SoC's debug components (CPUs, ETM, ITM, CTI, TPIU, etc.).
external_pins: SWCLK (Serial Wire Clock, host → target, input at target)
SWDIO (Serial Wire Data Input/Output, bidirectional, host ↔ target)
(Optional) nTRST — only present when the SWJ-DP variant exposes the SWJ-DP TRST connection at the SoC pin (rare in SWD-only parts)
(Optional) SWO — Serial Wire Output trace pin (separate from SWD protocol; carries ITM/DWT trace)
key_features: Two-wire reduced-pin debug interface: SWDIO (bidirectional data) + SWCLK (host-driven clock) replace the 4-wire JTAG TAP for resource-constrained MCUs.
SWJ-DP (Serial Wire / JTAG Debug Port) is mode-switchable between SWD and JTAG via a 16-bit selection sequence (JTAG-to-SWD = 0xE79E; SWD-to-JTAG = 0xE73C) on TMS/SWDIO.

Standard 46-bit SWD transaction: 8-bit Request (Start + APnDP + RnW + A[2:3] + Parity + Stop + Park) + 1-bit Turnaround + 3-bit Acknowledge (OK=001 / WAIT=010 / FAULT=100) + 33-bit Data field (32 bits + 1 parity) + 1-bit Turnaround.
Half-duplex per cycle: SWDIO is host-driven during Request and Data-Write phases, target-driven during ACK and Data-Read phases; explicit 1-bit Turnaround periods between direction changes.

ADIv5 Debug Access Port (DAP) two-layer architecture: Debug Port (DP) layer (the wire-level controller) + Access Port (AP) layer (up to 256 APs selected by APSEL register, each exposing its own 64-byte register window).
DP register catalog: ABORT (0x0 W), IDCODE/DPIDR (0x0 R), CTRL/STAT (0x4), SELECT (0x8 W), RDBUFF (0xC R), TARGETID (bank 2 ADIv5.1+), DLPIDR (bank 3 ADIv5.1+), EVENTSTAT (bank 4).

MEM-AP register catalog: CSW (Control & Status Word, 0x00), TAR (Transfer Address Register, 0x04), DRW (Data Read/Write, 0x0C), BD0-BD3 (Banked Data, 0x10-0x1C), MBT (Memory Barrier Transfer, 0x20), CFG (Configuration, 0xF4), BASE (ROM Table base, 0xF8), IDR (Identification, 0xFC).
JTAG-AP variant: forwards AP transactions over a downstream legacy JTAG TAP daisy chain — bridges ADIv5 DAP to legacy JTAG-only IP.
Auto-increment on TAR (CSW.AddrInc field): single-incrementing or packed-incrementing of the AP transfer address for sequential memory bursts.
WAIT retry: target returns WAIT (010) when busy; host must retry the same request. FAULT (100) signals a sticky error; host must read CTRL/STAT to identify the cause, write ABORT to clear, and retry.
Posted reads: the read data of the previous AP transaction is returned together with the ACK of the next transaction; the final read result is recovered via the DP RDBUFF register.
32-bit IDCODE / DPIDR register (post-reset readout): identifies the DP designer (JEP106 manufacturer ID), DP architecture revision, DP version, and minimum DP version supported.

CoreSight ROM Table at the MEM-AP BASE address: SoC publishes a hierarchical tree of debug components (CPUs, ETM, ITM, CTI, TPIU, ROM-of-ROMs, etc.); each entry has a present-bit + offset to a 4 KB component window.
Protocol-error escape: 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO held HIGH (the 'line reset') unconditionally resets the SW-DP back to a known state.
topology_summary: A single debug host (USB-to-SWD probe such as J-Link, ST-Link, CMSIS-DAP, Black Magic Probe, PE Micro, or ULINK) drives SWCLK out and tri-states/drives SWDIO bidirectionally to the target SoC's SWD-DP or SWJ-DP. The DAP sits between the wire-level SWD-DP and the on-chip Debug Bus (AXI / AHB / APB) reached via one or more APs (MEM-AP, JTAG-AP, etc.). The MEM-AP's ROM Table (CoreSight ROM Table, indexed by BASE) enumerates every debug component on the SoC. Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) allows two or more targets to share SWDIO/SWCLK with per-target selection via TARGETSEL.

revision_history.description: Initial release of ADIv5 alongside CoreSight; SW-DP / JTAG-DP / SWJ-DP defined; MEM-AP; JTAG-AP.
Added TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT registers; clarified Posted-Read semantics; tightened SWJ-DP selection-sequence definitions.
Multi-drop SWD: SWDIO/SWCLK shared between multiple SoCs with TARGETSEL-based per-target selection; refined DLPIDR fields; clarified line-reset sequence.

Successor architecture (Arm IHI 0074) — adds extended APs (APBv4-AP, AXI4-AP), 64-bit address support, hierarchical CoreSight ROM Tables; ADIv5 remains the baseline supported across all Cortex-M parts.

use_cases: Cortex-M (M0/M0+/M3/M4/M7/M33/M55) MCU in-system debug: halt/resume, single-step, breakpoints, watchpoints via DWT/FPB.
Cortex-M flash programming via the MEM-AP's AHB-Lite access to the on-chip flash controller.
CoreSight ITM / DWT printf-style trace readout (the SWO pin is separate but the SWO route is configured via the SWD-DP MEM-AP).
Power-on debug: reaching halt state before the application's first instruction executes.
Multi-core SoC debug: each Cortex core has its own MEM-AP slot in the DAP; CTI cross-triggers between cores.
Production / factory test of MCUs over the SWD pins (much smaller connector footprint than JTAG).
Multi-drop SWD daisy-chain probing of dual-core or multi-die SoCs from a single 2-pin connector (ADIv5.2).
overview: ARM Debug Interface v5 (ADIv5) is the universal debug-access architecture that every Arm Cortex-based SoC implements. The architecture is split into two layers: a wire-level Debug Port (DP) that brings transactions onto the chip, and an Access Port (AP) bus that fans those transactions out to one or more system buses on the SoC. JTAG-DP is the 4-pin (TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO) variant; SW-DP is the 2-pin (SWCLK/SWDIO) variant; SWJ-DP is a mode-switchable controller that supports both, selected at runtime via 16-bit JTAG-to-SWD (0xE79E) or SWD-to-JTAG (0xE73C) selection sequences shifted on TMS/SWDIO. The SWD protocol uses a strict 46-bit transaction format: an 8-bit host-driven Request packet (Start + APnDP + RnW + A[2:3] + Parity + Stop + Park), a 1-bit Turnaround, a 3-bit target-driven Acknowledge (OK=001 / WAIT=010 / FAULT=100), a 32-bit Data field plus 1 parity bit (host-driven for writes, target-driven for reads), and a final 1-bit Turnaround. Reads are posted — the read data returned in transaction N is actually the result of transaction N-1; the final read is recovered with a DP RDBUFF read. The DP exposes IDCODE/DPIDR, ABORT, CTRL/STAT, SELECT, RDBUFF, and (ADIv5.1+) TARGETID/DLPIDR/EVENTSTAT registers. The AP layer supports up to 256 APs selected via the APSEL field of the SELECT register; the canonical AP is MEM-AP (memory-mapped access via CSW + TAR + DRW + BD0-BD3 + CFG + BASE + IDR); JTAG-AP bridges to legacy JTAG TAPs. CoreSight ROM Tables published at the MEM-AP BASE address advertise the SoC's debug components.
block_diagram_components: Debug Host / SWD Probe (drives SWCLK; bidirectional SWDIO)
SWJ-DP Wire-Level Controller (mode-switchable SWD ↔ JTAG; SWD bit-shift register; 46-bit transaction state machine)
SW-DP / JTAG-DP Debug Port Layer (IDCODE/DPIDR + ABORT + CTRL/STAT + SELECT + RDBUFF + (ADIv5.1+) TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT)
Access Port Bus (selects up to 256 APs via SELECT.APSEL[7:0])
MEM-AP Instance(s) (CSW + TAR + DRW + BD0-BD3 + MBT + CFG + BASE + IDR; bridges DAP to system AHB/AXI/APB bus)
JTAG-AP Instance (forwards DAP transactions to a downstream legacy JTAG TAP daisy chain)
CoreSight Debug Bus (AHB / AXI / APB inside the SoC, reached by MEM-AP)
CoreSight ROM Table (publishes the SoC's debug component catalog at the MEM-AP BASE address)
Debug Components reachable via the bus (CPU debug registers, ETM, ITM, DWT, FPB, CTI, TPIU, ROM-of-ROMs)
Optional SWO trace pin output (separate output controlled via the MEM-AP-reachable TPIU)
industry_standard_basis: ARM IHI 0031C — ARM Debug Interface v5 Architecture Specification (and later IHI 0031D / IHI 0074 revisions). Maintained by Arm Limited. SWD is layered on top of ADIv5's Debug Port architecture and complements the 4-pin JTAG-DP variant defined by the same specification. CoreSight ROM Table format is defined by the companion CoreSight Architecture Specification (ARM IHI 0029).
